title: Punctual purity criterion for the relative Gysin class over a trait
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, and work on ordinary small-etale $D^+$ with signed Tate twists and ordinary compact-support right adjoints $p^!$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R$ is a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. Suppose $S$ is complete and strictly henselian (its local ring is henselian and its residue field is separably closed), of mixed characteristic, with $\ell$ invertible. Here henselian means simple roots of monic polynomials over the residue field lift to $R$. Let $p_T:T\to S$ be an integral regular finite-type quasi-projective scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^N_S$. A regular closed immersion has ideal locally generated by a regular sequence [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The virtual relative dimension $e_T$ of $p_T$ is $r-c$ in a local factorization as a regular closed immersion of codimension $c$ followed by a smooth morphism of relative dimension $r$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $K_T=p_T^!A_S(-e_T)[-2e_T]$.

Use the normalized Kummer class $c_T:A_T\to K_T$ of [lem-per-prepurity-lci-classes]. For each $t\in T$, let $T_t=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,t}$, $d_t=\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}$ and $i_t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\hookrightarrow T_t$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Say $T$ is punctually pure if every localized Kummer map
$$A_{\kappa(t)}\longrightarrow i_t^!A_{T_t}(d_t)[2d_t]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Then $T$ is punctually pure if and only if $c_T$ is an isomorphism. This includes schemes supported on the closed point of $S$; $p_T$ need not be flat.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.5.5 and proof, printed pp.248--249; punctual purity as in Definition 3.2.2.

proof.text: Work on a nonempty affine open $U$ of $T$. The trait $S$ is regular: its generic local ring is a field and its closed local ring has dimension one and a principal maximal ideal, so both satisfy [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $T$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] makes $U$ Noetherian. Regularity restricts because its local rings are unchanged; integrality restricts by the domain characterization in [def-pc-integral-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], the affine coordinate ring of $U$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra, so $U\to S$ is finite type. Apply [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] to this morphism of regular affine schemes $U\to S$: it factors as a regular closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow Y=\mathbf A^N_S$ followed by projection $q$. Here $q$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $N$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. Both $U$ and $Y$ are integral regular finite-type quasi-projective $S$-schemes: the coordinate ring of $Y$ is a polynomial ring over the domain $R$, and the displayed closed immersion gives quasi-projectivity of $U$. The intrinsic-dimension assertion of the geometric calculus and [lem-per-prepurity-lci-classes] give $e_U=e_T=N-c$, where $c$ is the codimension of $i$; thus $c$ is constant on $U$.

source.place: XVI, Proposition 3.5.5 proof, first sentence; affine-local version of the smooth/regular factorization.

proof.text: The ambient $Y$ is punctually pure. Indeed choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$ and specialize [lem-per-monomial-trait-punctual-purity] to $n=N+1$ and exponents $(1,0,\ldots,0)$. Its affine coordinate ring is $R[T_1,\ldots,T_{N+1}]/(T_1-\pi)$, identified with $R[T_2,\ldots,T_{N+1}]$ by substitution $T_1=\pi$ and the inverse inclusion of the remaining variables. This identifies the scheme in that statement with $Y$ and identifies its local rings and Kummer maps with those defining punctual purity on $Y$. The exponent tuple is nonzero, and zero exponents are expressly allowed. This also covers $N=0$, when the quotient is $R$. We use only this affine-space specialization of the existing node, not any assertion about the relative class $c_U$.

source.place: XVI, Proposition 3.5.2, printed p.248; the identical affine-space assertion is also the exponent-(1,0,...,0) specialization of Proposition 3.5.12, printed pp.250--251.

proof.text:
Write $\eta_i:A_U\to i^!A_Y(c)[2c]$ for the Kummer class. The smooth orientation [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation] gives the specified isomorphism $\gamma_q:A_Y(N)[2N]\xrightarrow{\sim}q^!A_S$. Its hypotheses hold: $Y$ and $S$ are Noetherian, $\ell$ is invertible, and affine space is separated and compactifiable by $\mathbf P^N_S$. Apply $i^!$, then shift and twist by $(-e_T)[-2e_T]$, and use exceptional transitivity [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition]. With $N-e_T=c$, this gives an isomorphism
$$b:i^!A_Y(c)[2c]\xrightarrow{\sim}p_U^!A_S(-e_T)[-2e_T]=K_U.$$
The signed Tate identifications are those of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Commuting a Tate line with $i^!$ can be checked on an etale cover trivializing that rank-one line, where the comparison is the identity, and these identities glue. The class composition formula of [lem-per-prepurity-lci-classes], with $e_i=-c$ and $e_q=N$, says exactly $c_U=b\circ\eta_i$. Its regular-immersion clause identifies the first factor with the normalized Kummer class of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], and its smooth clause identifies the second with this diagonal-class orientation. Therefore $c_U$ is an isomorphism if and only if $\eta_i$ is; this compares the actual maps with their fixed normalization.

source.place: XVI, Proposition 3.5.5 proof, commutative triangle and smooth Gysin isomorphism; composition is Theorem 2.5.12.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-punctual-purity-two-of-three] to $i:U\hookrightarrow Y$. Both schemes are regular Noetherian with $\ell$ invertible and $i$ has constant codimension $c$, as checked above. Its condition (c) holds because $Y$ is punctually pure at all its points by Step 2. Consequently its conditions (a) and (b) are equivalent: (a) and (c) imply (b), and (b) and (c) imply (a). In its notation (a) is exactly invertibility of $\eta_i$ and (b) is punctual purity of $U$. Combining with Step 3 proves that $c_U$ is an isomorphism if and only if $U$ is punctually pure.

source.place: XVI, Proposition 3.5.5 proof, last sentence, applying Proposition 3.2.3 and Corollary 3.5.3.

proof.text: Take an affine open cover by such $U$. Punctual purity of $T$ is equivalent to that of every $U$, since at a point $t\in U$ the local scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{U,t}$ is the same as $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,t}$, so the defining map is unchanged. By open restriction in [lem-per-prepurity-lci-classes], $c_T|_U=c_U$ under the canonical identification $K_T|_U=K_U$. A morphism in $D^+$ is invertible exactly when it is invertible on this open cover: apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] to its underlying abelian complexes, since every geometric point lies over a member of the cover and forgetting the $A$-module structure is exact and reflects isomorphisms. Step 4 now gives both implications globally. No step assumes that $T\to S$ is flat. In particular for $T$ supported on the closed point the same factorization works, and $e_T=N-c$ can be negative; all twist-shifts above are signed, so no case is excluded.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q107-86b502bb8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full, every cited statement, and ILO XVI 3.5.1–3.5.13 (printed pp.248–251). The delivery has no new nodes, the statement is unchanged, and the only stmt_dep change drops the unused def-weil-proper-morphism. The proof is the ILO 3.5.5 argument done on affine opens. Step 1: U↪A^N_S is a regular immersion by the regular-lci geometric calculus (all schemes Noetherian; U is integral, finite type and quasi-projective), and e_U=e_T=N−c by intrinsic virtual dimension, so c is constant. Step 2: the monomial node with (1,0,…,0) gives R[T]/(T_1−π)≅R[T_2..], which is A^N_S; zero exponents are allowed and N=0 gives S. Step 3: the prepurity composition formula with e_i=−c and e_q=N gives c_U=b∘η_i, with b iso via γ_q (smooth, separated, compactifiable by P^N, D^+). Step 4: two-of-three with (c) from Step 2 gives (a)⇔(b). Step 5: open restriction and stalk conservativity. I checked the edge cases N=0, c=0, T=S, and vertical T with e<0 (non-flat), and the routing: the per citations are on the unit, the other nodes are Mathlib/closed tools, and I accept the declared tool_uses (twist pullback, derived-stalk conservativity). There is no cycle and no SGA citation. Batch 5: the stmt-dep closure (through prepurity, which defines c_T) already contains all three flagged trf nodes, and the new citations add 0 trf/pod nodes. regular-sequence-dimension-formula is a Mathlib leaf (commutative algebra). finite-ring-section-deformation is the DNC smooth-orientation construction that defines c_T: neither assumption gives it, and Q06/Q64 accepted the same chain. bounded-below-derived-adjunction is the generic derivedPlus adjunction. All three are accepted. Maintainer notes: (1) ILO proves 3.5.12 using Cor 3.5.6, which rests on this item. When lem-per-monomial-trait-punctual-purity is split, its zero-exponent case must go through V(e)×A^m with smooth base change of pair purity and 3.5.13(iv), not through 3.5.6, or it creates a cycle. (2) Step 3's sentence on commuting Tate lines with i^! by local gluing is loose, but the prepurity composition clause (with its twist identifications) already covers it.
